newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KAISERSLAUTERN AT TOP AFTER BEATING HERTHA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KAISERSLAUTERN AT TOP AFTER BEATING HERTHA.

text.p: Newly-promoted Kaiserslautern went top of the German league on Wednesday with a 1-0 win against Hertha Berlin while champions Bayern Munich struggled to pick up their first point of the season.

Kaiserslautern, who beat Bayern four days ago in their opening game back in the top flight, maintained their 100 per cent record after two matches with a 74th-minute goal by Olaf Marschall in front of a 38,000 sell-out home crowd.

"We were a bit nervous in our game as the lads wanted to show that the win against Bayern was not a one-off. But we can be satisfied, two wins is the ideal way to start the season," Kaiserslautern coach Otto Rehhagel said.
European Cup winners Borussia Dortmund hammered Cologne 3-0 to move into second place, two points behind Kaiserslautern after their draw with Hertha at the weekend.
The goals for Dortmund came from Juergen Kohler, Heiko Herrlich and Joerg Heinrich.

Bayern were a goal down in the first half to Borussia Moenchengladbach, Swedish striker Joergen Pettersson scoring in the 17th minute, but midfielder Thomas Strunz saved their blushes with a 55th minute equaliser and a 1-1 draw.

Bayern were left near the bottom of the table but Italian coach Giovanni Trapattoni nonetheless put a brave face on the situation, noting that at least his men were beginning to show some attacking spirit.
"At least they had a lot of goal chances," he said.
